summary: The new up-to-60-second readiness wait in the prompt handler holds no upgrade permit, so a daemon handoff can end the HTTP request before the prompt is submitted.
A prompt that first arrives after the handshake has marked the record running, but before the first worker report sets capabilities.prompt, is still refused at once with 409.
Clean login discovery drops the Rust image's RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME, so rustup proxies in the agent-dev image look under /home/hel/.rustup instead of the installed toolchain.
The worker's clean re-exec drops the GH_TOKEN that container provisioning injects into the container environment, so configure_github_cli never writes the session token file at startup.
worker push-branch and diff re-exec with only the discovered login environment and do not restore the target's configured environment, so Git settings such as proxies are missing for branch export.
Login discovery runs '<shell> -l -c script', which csh/tcsh reject, and discovery is now mandatory, so accounts with a C-shell login shell cannot start workers.

Merging the cached login environment back under the prepared launch environment restores GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE entries that configure_github_cli removed after moving them into the worker Git config file.
The worker re-exec clears SSH_AUTH_SOCK inherited from the launcher, so SSH-agent-backed Git pushes from the worker may fail.
ACP terminal spawn removes GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN even when the terminal/create request supplies them explicitly.
For a legacy worker that does not lead its own process group, hel_kill_tree sends SIGKILL to the inherited launcher process group, bypassing the hel_group=legacy PID-only signaling.
A failed ps in hel_snapshot_tree yields an empty tree, because the pipeline status is awk's and '|| hel_tree=""' maps failure to empty, so the stop proceeds as if no descendants exist.
A descendant that starts a new process group after the one-time snapshot is not tracked, so the stop can report success while it still writes into the root.
Snapshotted PIDs/PGIDs are signaled without re-checking identity, so a PID or PGID reused within the grace period could be killed.
The controller's GitHub token is passed as `--env GH_TOKEN=<token>` in the podman/container (and ssh) command line, where other local users can read it.

The container bootstrap now installs `gh` whenever it is missing, so images that have Git but not `gh` and lack root/passwordless sudo (including the previous bundled image) fail provisioning even with no token or no GitHub repositories.

With a token, use_github_https_urls rewrites any source the lax owner/repo parser accepts, so a non-GitHub SCP URL such as `git@gitlab.com:team/repo` becomes `https://github.com/git@gitlab.com:team/repo.git`.
spawn_workspace_close reports the whole close as failed, without deleted_workspace_id, when the follow-up snapshot or workspace-list request fails after the daemon already deleted the workspace.

When one dashboard closes the default workspace, other connected dashboards skip composer disposal because only the initiator gets the deletion response, so they keep and later restore the discarded text.

discard_workspace_composers does not clear DashboardState::standby_prompts, so text typed into a standby composer during an attach survives the workspace close and is restored when the session is later reopened.

Snapshots written before native_session_used existed read it as false, and the earlier SessionOpened{resumed:true} or content evidence below the snapshot frontier is never replayed, so an imported or resumed thread with no local prompt can be silently replaced when its rollout is missing.

When the adapter offers session/load but not session/resume, the new missing-thread fallback opens session/new without setting session_updates_enabled, so every session/update from the replacement thread is dropped.

A successful resume marks the durable relay used but not the bridge's native_session_used atomic, so an in-process bridge restart keeps the stale startup value and can replace the thread if the next resume reports a missing rollout.
The wrapped quota row now reserves an unbounded number of rows, which can push out other rows on narrow or short terminals.
Concurrent model setups share one fixed .part path; the new remove-then-create lets one worker rename another worker's still-growing file into the installed location.
Direct downloads no longer create test_wavs, so the ignored end-to-end dictation test always panics on a fresh cache.
The setup status is shown only in the prompt block title, which ratatui clips on narrow terminals before the percentage and the Ctrl-R stop hint.
The reminder's idle check uses the completion snapshot, so a task submitted before the reminder is admitted makes the reminder run after that task and replace its valid report.
A handback request carries no originating turn, so a request replayed from the worker queue after a daemon outage is attributed to whatever turn is active then.
Queued configuration changes count as in-flight tasks, so the reminder is skipped and the turn is marked noticed even though no agent turn follows.
If the reminder is skipped because a prompt is queued and that prompt is then removed, the noticed turn is never reconsidered and waits treat the child as running.
A reminder submit that fails after the worker accepted it (lost acknowledgement) is recorded as failed, so a wait can return the last message while the reminder turn runs.
In ASCII mode a fractional quota cell below one half renders as nothing but still takes a cell away from empty_cells, so the bar is nine cells wide.

Composer hints are split on footer_separator(), which is " - " in ASCII mode, but the hint strings still contain literal " · ", so they form one item that keeps the Unicode dot and is dropped as a whole when space is short.

The transcript render cache and the second-opinion pane cache are keyed on width, mode and theme but not the symbol set, so changing Symbols in Setup leaves already rendered rows in the old glyph set.
truncate_line_to_width reserves one cell for the ellipsis, but the ASCII ellipsis ".." is two cells, so truncated output exceeds the requested width.
After two different failures stack, the displayed text holds the formatted count, so repeating the latest failure compares unequal and increments the count again although history drops the duplicate.
The Recent messages log truncates each notice to one row of the 80-column popup, so the end of a long failure message cannot be read anywhere.
The stacked-failure notice text uses a literal middle dot, so it shows Unicode under the ASCII symbol set.
Open conversations still draw hardcoded Unicode under ASCII: the voice button glyph, middle-dot separators in titles and metadata, and the em dash and ellipsis in the empty transcript.

When queued prompt B steers running prompt A, the projection switches active_turn to B and emits turn_started for B, but the worker later completes A, so turn_ended names A with no accepted ordinal and B never ends.
mj events polls Ctrl-C only around response.chunk(), and Tokio's SIGINT handler stays installed, so SIGINT cannot stop the command while it is blocked writing to a stalled stdout pipe.
The SSE endpoint returns 400 when after_seq and Last-Event-ID differ, which breaks a standard EventSource reconnect that keeps the original after_seq URL and sends a newer Last-Event-ID.

An upgraded or relaunched legacy macOS Claude session with Mjolnir sub-agents enabled loses Claude's Agent/Task tools while its linked home never received the mj-agents MCP config, so it has no delegation at all.

A legacy macOS Claude session with a non-default profile home actually ran from ~/.claude (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset), but the link points at the recorded custom home, so a relaunch uses different settings and history, or no link is made if that path is absent.

Checkpointing a still-running legacy local worker fails because the old launch.json memory root is under the real profile home while the controller now passes <worker_root>/profile, and the containment check is lexical.
A legacy session whose configured profile directory does not exist gets no link, so checkpoint and relaunch point at a missing staged home.

When the adapter exits right after SessionStarted, the runtime task's direct failed() can resolve the launch before the queued SessionStarted reaches the outer loop, and first-outcome-wins then reports a launch failure for a session that started.
Capping launch records at 64 evicts the oldest record even while it is still Starting, so its watcher gets 404s and reports a timeout.
Local path completion runs synchronous read_dir/is_dir outside the executor, so the 5 s deadline and cancellation never apply and a stalled mount pins one of the 4 shared preflight slots.
Arrow-key navigation in the suggestion list changes only aria-selected and never scrolls the selected row into the 40dvh scrolling list.
Suggestion buttons are in the tab order, and the input's blur handler removes them, so Tab from the field can drop focus instead of reaching the next control.
Recent skips every command that has a pane key, so Create session and Search sessions run from the palette never appear there.
Filtering prunes collapsed_project_keys for projects the filter hides, so clearing the filter re-expands them.
Pasted text is dropped while the Sessions search is being edited.
When the filter hides every row, focus moves to the Create action, plain becomes false, and Esc and the state letters are ignored.
select_active_session now checks the filtered list, so creating a session the active filter hides leaves the previous session selected while focus moves to the prompt.
The palette keeps the cursor on the previously selected command by id across query edits, so a weaker fuzzy match such as Stop session can remain selected below a better match and run on Enter.
`mj go` in a folder named `default` on a store whose built-in `default` row is empty now hits the new reserved-name refusal, because its naming path does not account for the reservation.
`mj new` reads the prompt and checks --bundle/--project-directory before the new missing-workspace refusal.
The refusal lists `default (0 sessions)` for a default workspace that is listed only because it holds stopped sessions, because session_count counts only active sessions.
A renamed `default` row disappears from the list once it has no sessions, and its new name is then refused as reserved.
The TUI chat can no longer scroll back past the 1,024-item window, because its background prefix conversion only uses the snapshot's transcript.
Dashboard unread counts drop agent messages and restarts that fall before the window, because the detail rebuilds them from the windowed transcript.
Once one turn exceeds 1,024 items, the dashboard loses the last user prompt excerpt and the latest activity after it, because the detail still scans the windowed transcript for the user message.
A 1,024-item window may give the browser fewer than 1,000 visible lines, because raw_only terminal entries are filtered after truncation.
Review seeds would lose the original task because the review host receives the truncated projection.
The SQL latest_user_position skips text-free user items while ProjectionWindow::of counts them, so the recovery observer could see an older turn.
The COUNT(*) for omitted_items scans every index entry of the session on each poll, and nothing in production reads it.
Raising shutdown_all_kills_running_terminal_commands' wait to 60s lets the 30s sleep/ping exit on its own, so the test no longer detects a shutdown that fails to kill the process.

Every spawn now passes a model to the start follow-up, and a Muse profile's only model is synthesized from settings.json and absent from its live ACP options, so a Muse child is registered and then fails before its first prompt on both spawn routes.

Explicit and inherited efforts are checked against the efforts of the chosen profile's default model rather than the requested model, so valid efforts are rejected and unsupported inherited ones make the child fail at startup.

spawn(model: "current") reads only snapshot.operational.config, which holds only explicitly applied selectors, so a parent running its harness default model is refused with 'current model is unknown', and its default effort is not inherited.

spawn now waits for discovery of every candidate profile, which may take up to 240s, while the MCP shim gives up after 120s, so a slow unrelated profile can turn a valid spawn into a tool error while the daemon still starts the child.
A busy-session deferral returns after the prestage has written a uniquely named checkpoint-stage-* directory, and nothing removes it, so repeated deferrals fill the target's disk.

An idle observation that arrives while the deferred copy still holds the recovery gate is dropped, and clearing last_attempted_turn later does not reconsider it, so the boundary can stay uncopied until some other view change.
A deferred manual checkpoint persists last_checkpoint_error = None and so wipes an existing checkpoint-failure warning, although the commit says deferral leaves the session row alone.
If a self-started harness turn begins before the daemon sees the prompted turn go idle, the watch is overwritten with prompt_driven=false and the prompted turn's automatic review never arms.
The wide minimized Sessions title shows only 'Attention: N' without the urgency glyph, so the badge loses the most-urgent level exactly at wide widths.

The new Unreachable level reaches notification_body, which has no arm for it, so a lost worker produces a desktop notification with the last agent message or 'Finished' instead of a connectivity failure.

The unreachable early return runs before the failed-review check, so a session with a failed review and an unreachable worker shows '?' and ranks below other failures, despite the Failed > Unreachable ladder.
When the post-restart lease fails, adopt_restarted_checkpoint_relay logs a warning and continues on an unleased standalone connection, bypassing the actor's lifecycle exclusivity.
The managed actor is unreserved for the whole dead-worker restart, so a prompt submitted then is dispatched to the new worker before the checkpoint leases and latches.
During and right after the restart, the unleased actor and the restart's StandaloneSession both project relay events into the same database, so one hits AlreadyApplied and Stop fails.
worker_connect_needs_restart does not recognize 'write relay hello request: Broken pipe', so a proxy that exits before the hello write skips the restart.
The pinned field title is drawn as an unwrapped one-row Paragraph and has been removed from the scrolling body, so a title wider than the pane is clipped and the rest cannot be read.
pin_accepted_codex_model merges only into the override map, so a CODEX_CONFIG exported by the login shell is replaced by a model-only object and its other keys are lost.
`mj resume --wiki <native-id> --json` prints the importer's progress lines on stdout before the JSON object, so stdout is not valid JSON.
The native-import branch ignores the indexed path and searches only the stock harness home, so sessions indexed from a configured profile's non-default home cannot be continued.

resume --wiki hardcodes both import acknowledgements to false and has no flags for them, so a noninteractive caller cannot continue a native session that has dirty repositories or omitted directories.

The restore branch always sends project_directory: None, and resume has no option to supply one, so an archived session with no indexed project directory (for example a container or bundle session) cannot be restored.
Without --workspace-id, the restore branch sends no workspace, the route turns it into an empty string, and session registration stores "" and fails validation, even when only one workspace exists.
apply_worker_summary replaces the summarized unread count but keeps unread_agent_message_sequences, so messages counted from live events before a reconnect are counted twice.
After the user reads a conversation, the poll targets keep the old viewed_through, so a later reconnect asks for a summary that counts already-read messages as unread.
A hydrated summary sets an unread count for the selected session even when its conversation is visible, bypassing the message_is_visible suppression the event path applies.
With only a 10-entry tail, a session whose last assistant message is outside the tail looks like it has no assistant history, so Delete destroys it without the typed confirmation.
The full bootstrap on Open advances the client cursor past events, including TurnCompleted, without passing them to recovery, so an automatic recovery checkpoint can be missed.
answer_reviewer starts a new self-rescheduling poll for the role, which already has one, so each answered form adds another permanent polling loop.
A poll that completes before the answer is recorded still lists the form as pending, so surface_reviewer_elicitations reopens the answered dialog, and nothing closes it later.

A session/new that fails or times out during the new readiness wait has already been inserted into `sessions`, so unanswered_refusal() suppresses the recorded refusal and mj acp exits 0 even though no session/new succeeded.
When the model or effort chip does not fully fit, its visible clipped part still renders with chip styling but gets no hitbox, so clicking it does nothing.
chip_limit leaves no room for the right-aligned activity spinner, so during a turn a chip hitbox can cover cells that the spinner overwrites, and clicking the spinner opens a selector.
A revocation can expire before a cookie issued under an earlier, longer session TTL if the TTL is later reduced.
When the revocation cannot be saved, the browser shows no error and no way to retry: the in-memory revocation forces the login screen, which hides the logout control.
Logout with a cookie that expired in transit skips revocation, so a renewed cookie from a delayed response can restore access.
Event streams opened before logout keep streaming after the viewer is revoked.
A panic in native_muse_turn unwinds and removes the temporary Muse profile while the adapter and native Muse process are still running.

The Refusal::precondition context is attached to every error from resolve_local_repository, so Git start failures, timeouts and cancellation become a 409 telling the caller to configure a remote, with no log reference.
A capacity refresh rejected because the poller stopped answers with reference 'capacity-poller', but no log entry records that reference.
Title-only or project-only search matches now come from a metadata scan that sets preview to None, so archived rows lose the preview text the resume dialog showed in their details.
The rename dialog looks the same whether the title field or the Save button has focus, but typing and Backspace only work while the field has focus.

In the new failed-session dialog, a long recorded error can push the explanation and the Cancel/Open transcript/Recover buttons below the clipped popup, with no scrolling, while Enter still activates the hidden focused button.
On a phone-width viewport with an empty composer, tabbing from the editor to Send or Attach removes composer-has-intent and hides the action row that is receiving focus.
The claim is that an existing 25dvh max-height and overflow on #conversation-side nests with the new 40dvh inner scroller on phones.
phone-layout.spec.js sets isMobile: true unconditionally, and Playwright's Firefox rejects that option, so the spec fails under the supported MJ_BROWSER_ENGINE=firefox setting.
The 15-second SAVE_ACK_TIMEOUT on config rename covers the local Controller reload too, so a slow reload after a successful rename is reported as an unacknowledged save.
On SshBare and AwsEc2 targets the controller records a relative dispatcher command while the worker compares it against an absolute root, so the owned review dispatcher is never preapproved.

When the source adapter supports session/resume but not loadSession, the replay restore falls back to a history-free resume that still emits SessionStarted{resumed:true}, and the import path treats it as a finished replay, closes the source and starts an empty primary.

A prompt submitted while the temporary import session is replaying is sent to the source runtime, which is shut down as soon as SessionStarted arrives, so the request is folded into the handoff without an answer and the destination is told to wait.
The new close-failure recovery dialog is never opened by the dashboard loop, and the 'x' force-destroy key was removed, so force destroy is unreachable from the dashboard.
The lossy annotation makes cross-harness profile choices wrap, but render_picker sizes the popup at one row per choice and cannot scroll, so later choices and the help text are clipped.
Adding session_contexts.workspace_id breaks existing tests that insert three positional values into the migrated table.
The version-13 migration test builds a v14 database and rewinds user_version to 12, so the non-idempotent v14 block reruns and fails with 'table workspaces already exists'.
delete_empty_workspace allows deleting the reserved 'default' workspace, after which every session-context insert (which relies on DEFAULT 'default') is aborted by the new insert trigger.
assign_new_session_workspace_at checks the current workspace and updates it in separate autocommit statements, so two concurrent assignments of the same default session can both succeed.
Any session still in 'default', including migrated ones, can be reassigned to another workspace despite the 'existing contexts are immutable' comment.
A name accepted by normalize_workspace_name can lowercase into a name_key longer than 64 characters, which the CHECK constraint then rejects.

muse_data_dir decides whether the profile home is the person's own Muse home by comparing paths as text, so a home that reaches ~/.config/muse through a symlink or another equivalent path is treated as a Mjolnir home and its saved model catalog is looked for under <home>/.data/muse.
Removing embedded_npm_recipes_match_the_runtime_pins leaves no check that the embedded Codex and Claude package.json files match the runtime pins.
Removing a_harness_restart_gates_dispatch_until_the_session_is_configured_again leaves the reset-and-reopen of the dispatch gate on bridge restart without a test.
Removing daemon_restart_without_a_baseline_does_not_hide_pending_work leaves no test that a relay restart without a review baseline does not create one.

The new SQL predicates use one-argument SQLite trim(), which strips only spaces, so a newline- or tab-only agent message counts as nonempty, unlike TranscriptItem::is_nonempty_agent_message, which uses Rust str::trim.

The startup summary's unread count is computed against the viewed cursor captured at spawn time and applied without recomputation, so a session read before the summary arrives shows its messages as unread again; an equal-ordinal summary can also overwrite an already-applied full projection.
last_materialized_user_message only considers items whose stable_id starts with 'user:' or 'user-', so a user item with a different ID would be skipped.

The supervisor publishes the exit status only after both pipes reach EOF, so a backgrounded child that inherits stdout/stderr keeps terminal/wait_for_exit pending and terminal/output reporting no exit after the shell has exited.
kill_if_live skips the group signal once the leader's exit is published, so a background process with redirected output survives terminal/kill, terminal/release and connection teardown.
shutdown kills and then awaits each terminal one after another with a 5 s timeout each, so stuck supervisors make teardown take N x 5 s and leave later groups unsignalled during that time.
shell_line passes the command verbatim to sh -c, so a command-plus-args request whose executable path contains spaces or shell metacharacters is parsed as shell syntax.

Terminals run in their own process groups and are supervised only inside the worker daemon, so stopping the daemon by signalling its process group leaves running terminal commands alive while cleanup removes the worker root or workspace.
Terminal children get the daemon environment plus the request's env, but not the session's configured environment (spec.environment) that the ACP agent receives.

The new cancellation gate reads the daemon's cached controller, which is refreshed every 500 ms, while the close task writes Destroying through its own Controller, so a cancel that arrives right after the durable transition is still accepted and can stop the target teardown.
session_projection holds the controller mutex and then calls active_lifecycles, which now locks the same non-reentrant std Mutex, so the daemon deadlocks on the first web publish.

On the new Stop-retry route, interrupted-close recovery can move a Closing record to Destroying (clearing last_error) and then fail without recording the error, so the TUI shows the record as an in-progress transition and blocks Stop.
Legacy Row{entry} positions are always read as indexes into the full transcript, but the previous build saved indexes into whatever was loaded, which is the tail when the prefix had not loaded yet.
same_installation now calls std::fs::canonicalize, and the TUI's setup_discovered calls setup_additions on the dashboard event loop, so a slow or hung filesystem can freeze the Settings UI.
When canonicalize fails, the lexical fallback collapses '..' after a symlink as if it were a plain directory, so two different homes can compare equal and discovery suppresses a real installation.

When canonicalize fails, the fallback does not resolve an existing symlinked prefix, so a home written through a symlink with a missing intermediate component still does not match its real path, and a duplicate is added.
Identity comparison now expands '~', but consumers use profile.home literally, so a '~' profile could suppress the discovered absolute profile that is the only one that works.
Provisioning creates the worker root with default mode before the worker runs, and create_owner_only_directory never tightens an existing directory, so new worker roots stay 0755.
owner_only_create_options binds `let mut options` unconditionally, but only a #[cfg(unix)] block mutates it, so Windows Clippy with -D warnings fails on unused_mut.
The ignored Docker integration test starts agent-dev:latest and asserts it has no worker, which fails as soon as this change publishes an image with the worker built in.
Recovery and parked sub-agent wake still use the host-binary digest gate, so they copy the host worker over the hel link to the image worker and fail when no host worker is available.
A dangling symlink at /opt/mjolnir/mj-worker fails `test -e` and is reported as absent instead of unusable.

Worker source copy, hash and fsync now runs before the daemon publishes its endpoint, so a slow capture exceeds the client's 8-second START_TIMEOUT and the launching CLI reports a startup failure; the copy also runs in full before the existing-digest check.
Every distinct local worker build is copied into a permanent workers/pinned/<digest>/ directory that nothing ever removes, so repeated rebuild-and-restart cycles grow disk use without bound.
Content-only digest reuses a cached artifact with stale non-executable permissions, so a local-bare worker install would keep failing after the source mode is fixed.

The post-stop check pipes ps into grep -F with the expanded match string, so ps can list the grep process itself and the script reports 'worker still running after stop' and exits 1 even when no worker remains.
A tight nested list merges the parent item's text into the child line under the child marker because Tag::List/Tag::Item does not flush the pending parent line.
Rich mode drops Markdown link destinations, showing only an underlined label that cannot be opened or seen without switching to raw mode.
A header-only table that is too wide for the viewport renders nothing, because the record fallback skips the header row and there are no data rows.
Table rows are joined without padding cells to column widths, so separators and values do not line up across rows.

The restore seed reads only the literal keys `model` and `effort` from the archived configuration, but that map is keyed by the harness's own option IDs (for example `reasoning_effort`), so those selectors are dropped on native resume.

The seed takes advertised current values from the archived projection rather than the relay's completed selections, so a provider default the user never chose is pinned as an accepted model or effort after resume.
Hel's ssh defaults are put in front of the user's ssh_args, and OpenSSH keeps the first value for each option, so users cannot override BatchMode, StrictHostKeyChecking or ConnectTimeout.

The ConnectTimeout=15 added in front of ssh_args overrides the 3-second ConnectTimeout that remote mount-path completion appends, so an unreachable host blocks the synchronous completion for about 15 seconds.
The new .unwrap_or(origin) shorthand fallback accepts non-GitHub SCP-style origins such as git@gitlab.com:team/repo.git as owner 'git@gitlab.com:team' and repository 'repo'.
hel import kimi --session is documented as taking the native session UUID, but the lookup compares it with the full 'session_<uuid>' directory name, so a bare UUID is never found.
Kimi --latest ranks sessions by the mtime of the session directory, which may not change when an existing session's files are appended or rewritten in place.

The Claude transcript reader never closes the final imported turn, so a session that ends on a user prompt or an interrupted response restores with the worker stuck in Running and rejecting new prompts.

Native-session import calls collect_git_snapshot without the reject_dirty_submodules guard that checkpoint export uses, so changes inside submodules are left out of the archive and nothing reports it.
Import uses the worktree's own HEAD as base_commit, so unpushed local commits are never bundled, and resuming into a fresh clone fails to check out the recorded HEAD.

The new .cargo/config.toml default target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl makes the existing bare cargo clippy/build/test CI steps build for a target whose standard library the CI does not install, on every OS.
Claims a relative or tilde workspace path is not normalized before the Claude slug and Kimi hash are derived on SSH/EC2 restores.

review_refs_metadata_only is set only when the raw capture found review refs, so a raw checkpoint without refs/mj refs still restores contents and can check out the archived commit in the shared checkout.
Raw archives no longer bundle review-ref objects but keep the same schema version (10), so an older reader that ignores the new flag may fail on a ref whose object is missing.
Ctrl-S while a Setup choice popup is open closes the combobox but the save is ignored, leaving a collapsed choice editor that Enter/click cannot reopen.
An open Model/Effort combobox keeps its numeric pending index when discovery replaces the option list, so Enter commits a different value.
Pointer hit testing does not give an expanded popup precedence, so clicks and wheel events on popup rows reach later-registered controls underneath.
Accepting an unchanged Code review combobox selection closes it internally but does not request a repaint, so the popup stays on screen.
The launch config sends only the marker's file name, so Kimi (credentials/kimi-code.json) and ZCode (v2/config.json) workers sync credentials at the wrong path.
Catalog cache rows use the same (profile, "") primary key as default-model discovery rows, so each overwrites the other.
A successful HTTP response is cached before it is parsed, so an invalid 200 body replaces the last usable catalog and breaks the outage fallback.
The required catalog step accepts only Codex's {"models": [...]} format, so a provider that serves the standard OpenAI {"data": [...]} list cannot launch.
Providers that use experimental_bearer_token get no staged catalog, and validation forbids a user catalog, so they keep OpenAI's built-in model list.
The catalog fallback uses the discovery cache's 24-hour expiry, so an outage more than a day after the last successful fetch still blocks launch.
ZCode quota now always reports 'no longer supported' while the ZCode harness still exists.
read_file passes the bare session's workspace_root (the project directory's parent) as --root, so project-relative paths resolve one directory too high, and siblings of the checkout become readable.
A bare session's file-read boundary is the checkout's parent, so sibling files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or other sessions' worktrees can be read.

The bundle export reads the checkpoint's committed bundle. For managed worktrees that bundle uses DeltaFrom(current HEAD), so it is always empty and the endpoint always answers 409 'no commits beyond the session base'.
For an unmanaged bare checkout the checkpoint uses MetadataOnly, so the bundle export always refuses with 'no commits beyond the session base'.
An unmanaged bare checkout gets neither --base nor --branch, so the new diff endpoint always fails with 'no session base recorded'.

For a session rooted in a repository subdirectory, capture_worktree_tree stages only `.` into an empty scratch index, so the diff against the full base tree reports every file outside the subdirectory as deleted.
Because the scratch index starts empty, `git add -A` skips tracked files that match ignore rules, so the session diff shows them as deleted.
diff_between_trees converts the patch with String::from_utf8_lossy, so a text diff of a non-UTF-8 file is corrupted in the exported patch.
Claims that managed network workspace bundles exclude commits already pushed to origin.
ReviewDispatch::launch drops each request's required hypothesis, so the specialist only ever receives the generic lane prompt and shared context.
In Recover mode, a terminated corrupt line longer than RELAY_EVENT_BYTE_BUDGET makes read_bounded_line fail, so the whole scan aborts instead of skipping the line and reporting a gap.
The Recover variant and gap fields are unused in non-test code, so `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` fails.
A prompt submitted while a config update is in flight is dropped by the runtime, but the UI has already recorded it and set turn=Streaming, so the UI stays stuck for the rest of the session.

refresh_config_picker keeps only clamped numeric indices, so a ConfigOptionUpdate that reorders or removes options while the picker is open can make Enter apply a value to a different option or apply a different value.
The modal height is rows+4, but the inner layout needs header 2 + list + footer 1 plus 2 border rows, so each picker is one row short.
